faq: Does it replace my current search?
It can, or it can sit beside it. Many clients start by adding it as the main box and keeping the old search as a fallback for a week. We agree which approach suits you before we build.
Will it work with Shopify or WordPress?
Yes. We connect to your product or content data through the platform's own tools, and we add the search box to your theme. For custom sites we need to see how your content is stored first.
What does it cost to run?

Search usually costs little per query. Some tools bill by the month and some by use, always through your own account. We estimate the monthly cost for your traffic and explain it in the handover notes.

You choose. By default we show them lower in the results with a clear label, or hide them. We set this up using your stock data and explain how to change the rule.

desc:
Smart search for websites and stores lets visitors type a question the way they would ask a person and still reach the right product or page. Ecom Swift LLC builds it over your own catalog or content, tunes the ranking and styles the results to match your site.

## What is smart search for a website or store?

Smart search is a search box that understands meaning, not only matching words. A traditional box looks for the exact letters typed. If a shopper types "something warm for hiking" and your product is titled "insulated trail jacket", a keyword search may return nothing. A smart search compares the meaning of the question with the meaning of your items and returns the jacket.

It also copes with typos, plurals, synonyms and full sentences, which is how people really search on a phone.

## Why basic site search loses visitors

Visitors who use the search box are often the most interested ones. They know what they want and are asking for it directly. A page with no results sends them away, usually to a competitor or a general search engine.

Basic search fails in common ways. It cannot handle spelling mistakes, it does not know that a couch is a sofa and it ranks items by word count rather than relevance. Shop owners rarely see these failures, because nobody reports a search that returned nothing.

## How better search affects results

When search works, shoppers find products faster and readers find articles without scrolling menus. Fewer dead ends mean fewer people leaving at the point where they showed intent. The mechanism is straightforward: a clearer path from a need to the right page.

Search data is a second benefit. A report of what visitors typed, and which searches found nothing, tells you which products to stock, which pages to write and which words your customers actually use.

## What a good search set-up includes

- An index built from your products, pages or articles, with the fields that matter.
- Understanding of plain-language questions and long phrases.
- Typo and synonym handling, with a list you can extend.
- Filters by price, type or category, where your data supports them.
- Suggestions that appear as people type.
- Short written answers shown above the results, when they help.
- Ranking controls that let you pin or boost chosen results.
- Out-of-stock handling that you decide, such as showing last or hiding.
- A scheduled refresh, so new items appear without manual work.
- A report of searches that returned nothing, sent to you regularly.

## What we do

We begin with your data. We load products or content into a search index, check that titles, descriptions and categories are usable and set the ranking rules. We style the box and results to match your theme, then run a tuning round with test searches that you provide.

The Basic package covers a smarter box over a limited set of items. The Standard package adds more items, filters, suggestions, a zero-result report and a tuning round. The Premium package indexes more, adds written answers above results, pinning and boosting, nightly updates, a weekly email report and a handover guide. The search can replace your current box or sit beside it, and we agree which with you first.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Write clear product titles and descriptions, since search reads them.
- Collect real searches from customers and use them as test cases.
- Review the zero-result report every week.
- Decide how to treat out-of-stock items before launch.
- Keep a visible link to your contact page on the results screen.

**Avoid:**
- Pinning too many results, which hides relevant ones.
- Indexing hidden, draft or private pages.
- Adding a written answer when your content does not support one.
- Judging the tool on one search only.
- Forgetting that ongoing usage has a running cost.

## Who it is for

An online store with hundreds of products finds that shoppers cannot find items by description. A publisher with years of articles wants readers to search by question. A service business with a detailed site wants visitors to land on the right page quickly.

## What we need from you

We need the address of your site, access to your product or content data and your platform, shared as a collaborator, staff or developer user where supported. Never send a password. Tell us about typical searches, words customers use and any items that must always appear first. We work with common platforms such as Shopify and WordPress and confirm fit before we start.
